title: RFM Analysis: The Ultimate Guide to Ranking Customer Value - Rejoiner

facts.fact: The article's RFM method scores each dimension (recency, frequency, monetary) from 1 to 5 by splitting the customer database into quintiles of 20% each.
facts.quote: break up the database into quintiles (Top 20%, Second 20%, etc) and assign a score of 1-5 to each customer

facts.fact: In the article's RFM scoring, a customer with a combined rank of 555 is the most recent, most frequent, and highest monetary spender.
facts.quote: The customer with a rank of 555 is your most recent, most frequent, and biggest monetary spender.

facts.fact: In the article's RFM scoring, a customer with a combined rank of 111 is the opposite of the 555 customer and is described as probably not worth marketing to.
facts.quote: A customer with a rank of 111 is the opposite (and probably not worth marketing to).

facts.fact: The article defines recency for eCommerce companies as typically measured in days since the customer's last purchase.
facts.quote: For eCommerce companies, this is typically measured as days since last customer purchase.

facts.fact: The article defines frequency as the sum of a customer's purchases over their lifetime.
facts.quote: Frequency score is calculated based on the sum of purchases throughout a customer's lifetime.

facts.fact: The article defines monetary value as the sum of revenue a customer spends over their lifetime.
facts.quote: The sum of revenue a customer spends in their lifetime.

facts.fact: According to the article, RFM segmentation was first used by direct marketers sending catalogs by direct mail in the 1930s and 1940s.
facts.quote: RFM segmentation was first employed by direct marketers sending catalogs via direct mail in the 1930s and 1940s.

facts.fact: According to the article, catalogers in the 1930s and 1940s maintained a 3x5 index card for every customer in their file to rank customers by RFM.
facts.quote: Catalogers would maintain and update a 3×5 index card for every customer in their file.
